text: A naive in-memory vector store keeps every vector in a Python dictionary and computes cosine similarity against every record during search.
Normalized vector search precomputes unit vectors at insert time so that search can use a dot product instead of cosine similarity.
A matrix-backed vector store stores vectors in a contiguous NumPy matrix and performs search using vectorized matrix multiplication.
Buffered matrix stores improve insert performance by collecting new vectors in a small buffer before merging them into the main matrix.
Exact vector search scans all records and returns the true nearest neighbors according to the chosen similarity function.
A file-backed vector store persists records to disk so that vectors and metadata can survive process restarts.
Tombstones mark deleted records without immediately rewriting the entire vector file.
Compaction rewrites live records and removes tombstoned records from physical storage.
Memory-mapped vector storage can improve read performance by allowing large vector matrices to be accessed without loading everything eagerly.
Metadata filtering restricts search results to records whose metadata matches the requested constraints.
Approximate nearest neighbor search trades a small amount of recall for lower query latency on large vector collections.
IVF partitions vectors into clusters using centroids and searches only a subset of inverted lists during query time.
The nlist parameter controls how many clusters are created in an IVF index.
The nprobe parameter controls how many IVF clusters are searched for each query.
If nprobe is too low, IVF may miss relevant vectors that are located in neighboring clusters.
NSW graph search connects vectors to nearby neighbors and performs greedy traversal through the graph.
HNSW improves graph search by adding multiple layers, where upper layers provide long-range shortcuts and lower layers provide detailed local search.
The ef_search parameter controls how broadly HNSW explores candidate nodes during search.
The ef_construction parameter controls how much work HNSW does while building graph connections.
Graph-based ANN indexes often expose diagnostics such as visited nodes, graph hops, and distance computations.
A semantic retriever embeds user queries and text chunks into the same vector space before performing similarity search.
PDF ingestion extracts text from pages and splits it into chunks before embedding and indexing.
Chunking strategy affects retrieval quality because very small chunks may lose context while very large chunks may include too much unrelated text.
Retrieval augmented generation uses retrieved chunks as context for a language model to answer user questions.
Poor retrieval can cause a RAG system to miss important facts or include irrelevant context.
Retrieval quality evaluation compares retrieved results against human-labeled relevant documents.
Recall at K measures how many relevant documents were retrieved within the top K results.
Precision at K measures how many of the top K retrieved results are actually relevant.
Mean reciprocal rank measures how early the first relevant result appears in the ranked list.
nDCG rewards highly relevant documents appearing earlier in the ranked results and supports graded relevance labels.
Maximal marginal relevance balances query similarity with diversity so that retrieved chunks are not overly repetitive.
